<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

After plan 180 (#73, live 2026-10-28) the machine daemon still launches ~13 processes/s, essentially all `ps.proc-liveness`: `ProcLiveness::proc_start` runs `/bin/ps -o lstart= -p PID` for every liveness check (the 5 s death sweep over every live seat, plus whoami/request paths). Defender's EDR inspects every launch. pij-fleet#74 (Vaughan) proposes: (1) read the start time in-process; the workspace forbids unsafe_code, so macOS needs a vetted dependency and an ADR; (2) resolve `git` and `tmux` through PATH once per daemon instead of a posix_spawnp PATH search per launch (12 kernel-process misses each on a 32-entry PATH). Semantics must not change: no TTL or cache of liveness (plan 180 R8 rejected one). Rulings: assets/rulings.md.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- `ps.proc-liveness` is 0 in `pij-rs ping`, with identical liveness answers.
- git and tmux launches no longer search PATH each time.
- Any new dependency is chosen on the record (ADR).

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Caching liveness answers or adding a TTL.
- Changing the death sweep's cadence or the reaper's rules.
- Other launch sites (they are rare; name any you find for a follow-up).

## Acceptance criteria

| id | claim | state | note | receipt | pressure | proven_by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ac-0001 | In-process liveness. `ProcLiveness::proc_start` (crates/harnesses/src/proc.rs) reads a process's start time with no process launch, on macOS (sysctl KERN_PROC_PID / kinfo_proc p_starttime, or proc_pidinfo) and Linux (/proc/&lt;pid&gt;/stat field 22 plus btime, std only). Every caller gets the same answer it got from `/bin/ps -o lstart=`: parity tests for this process, a child, a dead PID and a PID whose start time differs (the recycled-PID case), at the precision the comparison uses. No TTL, no cache (R1). | [ ] unchecked | — | — | [bp-0001](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | — |
| ac-0002 | Dependency on the record. If macOS needs a crate (unsafe_code stays forbidden in the workspace), docs/adr/ gets an ADR comparing at least two candidates and the std-only alternatives: licence, maintenance and download history, transitive dependencies, build scripts, unsafe surface, and a release at least 7 days old (R2). The chosen crate is pinned, added to crates/testkit/arch-allowlist.toml, and the lockfile and audit gates pass. Linux uses std only. | [ ] unchecked | — | — | [bp-0001](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | — |
| ac-0003 | Resolve git and tmux once. The daemon resolves `git` and `tmux` through its PATH on first use and launches the resolved absolute path afterwards. Only a found path is kept, never a miss, so a tool installed after boot is found. The first PATH match still wins (a decoy-on-PATH test, as in crates/harnesses/tests/path_search.rs). `crates/testkit/tests/spawn_sites.rs` is extended so a bare `git`/`tmux` launch in the daemon crates fails. | [ ] unchecked | — | — | [bp-0001](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | — |
| ac-0004 | Cost (AGENTS.md § Resource cost). Steady state: the death sweep and request paths launch nothing for liveness. Live before/after receipts: two `pij-rs --json ping \| jq .data.spawns` readings 20 s apart and `just spawn-rate --seconds 20`, before on main and after on the branch build where possible; the prime takes the deployed after-reading. `ps.proc-liveness` goes to 0, and no new per-tick launch appears. | [ ] unchecked | — | — | [bp-0002](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | — |
| ac-0005 | Docs. docs/how/macos-defender.md § What pij does about launches describes in-process liveness and resolve-once, with the new numbers; the ADR is linked. | [ ] unchecked | — | — | [bp-0002](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | — |
